profile.feeling: Home and property — in today’s China also the big life goal of owning a flat.

senses.def: house; a building to live in
a flat, a home (as property: 买房子)

examples.py: Zhè shì yí dòng lǎo fángzi.

examples.text: 他们在城里买了一套房子。
examples.py: Tāmen zài chéng lǐ mǎile yí tào fángzi.
examples.tr: They bought a flat in the city.

phrases.tr: house slave

synonyms.nuance: ‘home’ — the family place, not the building: 我回家 ‘I’m going home’

etymology.text: 房 ‘room, house’ (户 ‘door’ + phonetic 方) + the toneless noun suffix 子.

funFacts: In mainland cities most people live in flats, so 买房子 ‘to buy a house’ usually means buying a flat — counted with 套 ‘set (of rooms)’.
pitfalls: ‘Home’ is 家: 我回家 ‘I go home’ — not *我回房子.
Measure words: 一栋 / 一座 / 一所房子 for a building, 一套房子 for a flat.
subtleties: In some regions 房子 also means a single room: 一间房子.

profile.feeling: A flat in a block — often rented, serviced or for students.

examples.py: Tā zhù zài yí tào xiǎo gōngyù li.
examples.tr: She lives in a small flat.

examples.py: Zhè dòng gōngyù yǒu èrshí céng.
examples.tr: This block of flats has twenty floors.

synonyms.nuance: the everyday word for one’s home — mainland speakers rarely call their own flat 公寓
a flat in a residential block (mainland)
a self-contained flat or a hotel suite
a multi-storey building, as opposed to a one-storey house

etymology.text: 公 ‘public, common’ + 寓 ‘to lodge; residence’ (宀 ‘roof’ + phonetic 禺).

funFacts: In Taiwan 公寓 is the classic walk-up block of four or five floors without a lift, as opposed to a 大樓 with a lift.
pitfalls: Mainland speakers usually say 我家 or 我的房子 for their own flat; 公寓 suggests a rented or serviced apartment.
Measure words: 一套公寓 ‘a flat’, 一栋公寓 ‘a block of flats’.
subtleties: 学生公寓 are university halls of residence.

profile.feeling: A room of your own — at home or in a hotel.

senses.def: room (in a house, flat or hotel)

examples.py: Zhège fángjiān yǒu liǎng zhāng chuáng.
Nǐ hǎo, wǒ xiǎng dìng yí ge fángjiān.
examples.tr: Hello, I’d like to book a room.

synonyms.nuance: short form in compounds: 书房 ‘study’, 厨房 ‘kitchen’
written ‘room’ in compounds: 卧室 ‘bedroom’, 教室 ‘classroom’

etymology.text: 房 ‘room, house’ + 间 ‘space between; room’ — 间 is also the measure word for rooms.

funFacts: Rooms are named with 房 or 室: 厨房 kitchen, 书房 study, 卧室 bedroom, 浴室 bathroom.
pitfalls: ‘In the room’ needs 里: 在房间里 — not just *在房间.
subtleties: Hotels sell 单人间 (single rooms) and 双人间 (double rooms) — 间 again.

profile.feeling: Coming and going — the way in and out.

senses.def: measure word for school subjects and languages (一门课)

examples.py: Wǒ zhège xuéqī yǒu wǔ mén kè.
examples.tr: I have five courses this semester.

collocations.tr: to open the door; to open (a shop)
to close the door; to close

phrases.tr: open the door and see the mountain
phrases.meaning: to come straight to the point

phrases.tr: the doors match, the houses match
phrases.meaning: a marriage between families of equal standing

synonyms.nuance: the main door or gate of a building or compound
a single door; today in words like 窗户 and 户口 ‘household’

etymology.text: Pictogram of a gate with two leaves; 户 ‘a (single) door’ is half of it.

funFacts: Shops 开门 ‘open the door’ in the morning and 关门 ‘close the door’ at night — the same words mean ‘open’ and ‘closed’, and 关门 also ‘go out of business’.
pitfalls: Measure words: 一扇门 (a door panel), 一道门 (a doorway, a gate); 个 is common in speech.
subtleties: The simplified 门 comes from the cursive form of 門; the radical appears in 们, 问, 间 and 闻.

profile.feeling: Light and air; a view out.

examples.tr: Outside the window there is a park.
The eyes are the windows of the soul.

phrases.tr: the eyes are the windows of the soul
phrases.meaning: you can read someone’s heart in their eyes

phrases.tr: open the skylight and speak in the light

synonyms.nuance: short form, usual in writing and compounds: 窗前, 窗外, 窗台
a service window, a counter; a window on a computer screen

etymology.text: 窗 ‘window’ (穴 ‘hole’ + 囱) + 户 ‘(single) door’, toneless: chuānghu.

funFacts: 窗口 is both the ticket window at a station and a window on a computer screen.
pitfalls: The second syllable is toneless: chuānghu.
Measure word: 一扇窗户, like doors.
subtleties: In writing and poetry the short 窗 is preferred: 窗前 ‘in front of the window’.

profile.feeling: Solid, separating, protecting — also the barrier around the Chinese internet.

senses.def: (internet slang) the Great Firewall — 翻墙 ‘to climb over the wall’

examples.py: Qiáng shang yǒu yì zhāng huà.
examples.tr: There is a picture on the wall.

examples.py: Zhè miàn qiáng shì báisè de.
Tā měi tiān fān qiáng kàn xīnwén.
examples.tr: Every day he gets around the firewall to read the news.

collocations.tr: to climb the wall; to get around the firewall

phrases.tr: grass on top of a wall
phrases.meaning: a fence-sitter, someone who bends with the wind

phrases.tr: a cornered dog will jump over a wall

synonyms.nuance: a wall around a courtyard or compound

etymology.text: Traditional 牆: phonetic 爿 + semantic 嗇 ‘wheat in a granary’; the simplified 墙 takes 土 ‘earth’ as its semantic part.

funFacts: The Great Wall is 长城 ‘the long city-wall’ — 城 originally meant a city wall.
pitfalls: ‘On the wall’ is 墙上 (wall + on): 墙上有一张画.
subtleties: Measure words: 一面墙 or 一堵墙; a long wall can be 一道墙.

profile.feeling: Meals together and work — the centre of a Chinese home is the dining table.

examples.py: Zhuōzi shang yǒu yì běn shū.
examples.tr: There is a book on the table.

examples.py: Wǒmen huàn yì zhāng dà zhuōzi ba.
examples.tr: Let’s change to a bigger table.

phrases.tr: to bang the table

synonyms.nuance: short form; also the measure word for tables of guests: 二十桌客人

etymology.text: 桌 from 卓 ‘high’ with 木 ‘wood’ — the table is the tall piece of furniture — + the toneless suffix 子.

funFacts: At a banquet guests are counted in tables: 我们请了二十桌 ‘we invited twenty tables (of guests)’.
pitfalls: ‘On the table’ = 桌子上.
Measure word 张 (for things with a flat top): 一张桌子 — 套 only for a set of furniture.
subtleties: A desk is 书桌 ‘book table’; a round table, 圆桌.

profile.feeling: A seat with a back to lean on.

examples.py: Fángjiān li yǒu sì bǎ yǐzi.
examples.tr: There are four chairs in the room.

examples.py: Zhè bǎ yǐzi zuòzhe hěn shūfu.
examples.tr: This chair is comfortable to sit on.

synonyms.nuance: ‘seat, place’ — in a bus, cinema, classroom

etymology.text: 椅 from 倚 ‘to lean’ (木 ‘wood’ + phonetic 奇) — the seat you lean back on — + the toneless suffix 子.

funFacts: Chinese people sat on mats on the floor until chairs spread during the Tang and Song dynasties.
pitfalls: The usual measure word is 把 (a chair is ‘held’ by its back like a handle): 一把椅子; 张 is also used.
A seat without a back is 凳子, not 椅子.
subtleties: ‘To sit on a chair’ is 坐在椅子上 — 在 + chair + 上.

profile.feeling: Rest and comfort at the end of the day.

senses.def: (classical) couch, seat; possibly the railing of a well

examples.tr: The children are already in bed.

examples.py: Wǒ měi tiān qī diǎn qǐchuáng.
examples.tr: I get up at seven every day.

phrases.text: 床前明月光，疑是地上霜。
phrases.tr: Before my bed the bright moonlight — I take it for frost on the ground.
phrases.meaning: the opening of the most famous Chinese poem, learnt by every child
phrases.source: Li Bai (李白), 静夜思 ‘Quiet Night Thoughts’ (8th century)

synonyms.nuance: ‘bed, berth’ — beds as furniture or in dormitories
kàng: the heated brick bed of northern China

etymology.text: 广 ‘house’ + 木 ‘wood’: a wooden piece of furniture in the house; originally a variant of 牀.

funFacts: Scholars still argue whether the 床 of Li Bai’s poem is a bed or the railing of a well — an old meaning dictionaries also record.
pitfalls: 上床 ‘to go to bed’ is also a euphemism for sex; ‘go to bed (to sleep)’ is safer as 睡觉.
subtleties: 起床 is ‘to get up’ — literally ‘rise from the bed’.

profile.feeling: Storage: doors, shelves, things put away.

examples.tr: The cups are in the cupboard.

examples.py: Wǒmen xūyào yí ge xīn guìzi.

etymology.text: 柜 (traditional 櫃: 木 ‘wood’ + phonetic 匱 ‘box’) + the toneless suffix 子.

funFacts: 出柜 ‘to come out of the cupboard’ is the Chinese for coming out as gay — a calque of the English ‘come out of the closet’.
pitfalls: ‘In the cupboard’ is 柜子里.
A wardrobe for clothes is more precisely 衣柜.
subtleties: 柜台 (shop counter) and 保险柜 (a safe) contain the same 柜 ‘box, cabinet’.

profile.feeling: Clothes hanging inside — the bedroom cupboard.

examples.tr: The clothes are all in the wardrobe.

examples.py: Wǒ de yīguì tài xiǎo le.
Wǒmen mǎile yí ge xīn yīguì.

synonyms.nuance: ‘wardrobe’ — a common alternative, especially in writing

etymology.text: 衣 ‘clothes’ (a pictogram of the collar and front of a garment) + 柜 ‘cabinet’.

funFacts: 衣 is a picture of the collar and front of a garment; as a component it becomes 衤, as in 衬衫 ‘shirt’.
pitfalls: 衣柜 is only for clothes; dishes go in a 碗柜 or 橱柜.
subtleties: Chinese often name furniture by what it holds: 衣柜 ‘clothes cabinet’, 书柜 ‘book cabinet’, 鞋柜 ‘shoe cabinet’.

profile.feeling: Light in the dark — warm lamps, red lanterns, traffic lights.

examples.py: Fángjiān li yǒu yì zhǎn dēng.
examples.tr: There is a lamp in the room.

phrases.tr: red lanterns and green wine
phrases.meaning: a life of luxury and dissipation

synonyms.nuance: ‘lantern’ — paper or silk, red at festivals

etymology.text: Traditional 燈: 火 ‘fire’ + phonetic 登; the simplified 灯 (火 + 丁) is an old character adopted for it.

funFacts: The Lantern Festival (元宵节) ends the New Year season with lanterns, 灯笼, everywhere.
pitfalls: ‘Turn the light on / off’ is 开灯 / 关灯 — 开 and 关 work for all devices.
Measure word 盏: 一盏灯 (个 in speech).
subtleties: 灯 covers lamp and light: the device and the light it gives.

profile.feeling: Learning, culture and quiet reading — books are highly respected.

senses.def: letter, document (in compounds: 情书 ‘love letter’)

phrases.tr: a gate with the fragrance of books
in books there are houses of gold

synonyms.nuance: ‘notebook, exercise book’ — not a book to read

etymology.text: Traditional 書: 聿 ‘writing brush’ + phonetic 者; the simplified 书 comes from its cursive form.

funFacts: 读书 ‘to read books’ also means ‘to go to school, to study’: 他还在读书 ‘he is still a student’.
pitfalls: Measure word 本: 一本书, never *一个书 in careful speech.
看书 ‘look at books’ is the everyday ‘to read’.
subtleties: 部 counts a book as a work: 一部小说 ‘a novel’.

profile.feeling: Writing — from the ink brush to the ballpoint.

senses.def: measure word for sums of money and deals (一笔钱)

examples.py: Zhè zhī bǐ bù hǎo xiě.
Tā jièle yí dà bǐ qián.
examples.tr: He borrowed a large sum of money.

phrases.tr: a wonderful brush brings forth flowers

etymology.text: Traditional 筆: 竹 ‘bamboo’ + 聿 ‘writing brush’; the simplified 笔 is 竹 ‘bamboo’ + 毛 ‘hair’ — what a brush is made of.

funFacts: The simplified character tells you what a Chinese brush is: bamboo (竹) + hair (毛).
pitfalls: 笔 alone is any pen; the kinds are compounds: 铅笔 pencil, 钢笔 fountain pen.
Measure word 支: 一支笔.
subtleties: 支 and 枝 are both written as its measure word; 支 is the mainland standard.

profile.feeling: Plain and useful — and one of China’s great inventions.

examples.py: Qǐng gěi wǒ yì zhāng zhǐ.
examples.tr: Please give me a sheet of paper.
This kind of paper is thin.

phrases.tr: to discuss warfare on paper
paper tiger
phrases.meaning: something that looks threatening but is weak

etymology.text: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 糸 ‘silk’ (the radical of textiles) + phonetic 氏.

funFacts: English ‘paper tiger’ is a calque of the Chinese 纸老虎.
Papermaking is one of China’s ‘Four Great Inventions’; Cai Lun (蔡伦) improved it around 105 CE. English paper and German Papier come from Greek πάπυρος ‘papyrus’ — a different material.
pitfalls: Paper is counted by the sheet: 一张纸 ‘a sheet of paper’ — no 个.
subtleties: 纸 is in many words: 报纸 newspaper, 纸币 banknote, 剪纸 paper-cutting.

profile.feeling: Always in your hand — phone, wallet and map in one.

examples.py: Wǒ de shǒujī méi diàn le.
Nǐ de shǒujī hàomǎ shì duōshao?

examples.tr: Stop playing on your phone all the time!

phrases.tr: the head-down tribe
phrases.meaning: people always looking down at their phones

synonyms.nuance: ‘telephone’ — also used for the mobile, and for the call or the number
the brick-sized mobile phone of the late 1980s and 1990s

etymology.text: 手 ‘hand’ (a pictogram of a hand with fingers) + 机 ‘machine’ (traditional 機): the ‘hand machine’.

funFacts: German calls it das Handy — Chinese 手机 is also a ‘hand’ word.
pitfalls: Measure word 部 or 台 (个 in speech): 一部手机.
‘Mobile number’ is 手机号 or 手机号码.
subtleties: With apps such as WeChat (微信) the phone is also a wallet: 用手机付钱 ‘pay with the phone’.

profile.feeling: Calls and numbers — the telephone and what you do with it.

examples.tr: The telephone is on the table.

etymology.text: 电 ‘electricity’ (originally ‘lightning’: 雨 ‘rain’ + 申, a picture of a lightning bolt) + 话 ‘speech, words’ (言 ‘word’ + phonetic): ‘electric speech’.

funFacts: Greek τηλέφωνο is ‘far voice’, the old official German Fernsprecher ‘far speaker’ — Chinese 电话 is ‘electric speech’.
pitfalls: ‘To call someone’ is 给 + person + 打电话: 我给你打电话 — 打 ‘hit’ is the verb.
subtleties: In speech 电话 often means the call or the number rather than the device.

profile.feeling: Small but important — getting in, and the key to a problem.

examples.tr: Cooperation is the key to success.

phrases.tr: one key opens one lock
phrases.meaning: every problem needs its own solution

synonyms.nuance: ‘key’ in the south and in Cantonese-speaking areas

etymology.text: 钥 (金 ‘metal’ + phonetic 龠) + 匙 ‘spoon’ (匕 ‘spoon’ + phonetic 是).

funFacts: 匙 alone means ‘spoon’ (汤匙 tāngchí ‘soup spoon’); in 钥匙 it is a toneless shi.
pitfalls: 钥 is read yào here; the second syllable is toneless: yàoshi.
Measure word 把, as for things held by a handle: 一把钥匙.
subtleties: 钥匙 is both singular and plural: ‘my keys’ is still 我的钥匙.

profile.feeling: Everyday and practical — what you carry; also the word for wrapping.

senses.def: to wrap (verb: 包饺子 ‘to make dumplings’)

examples.py: Tā mǎile yí ge xīn bāo.

phrases.tr: to wrap up ten thousand things

synonyms.nuance: ‘bag, sack’ — of plastic, paper or cloth
‘bag’ in a cute, childlike way — also used for handbags

etymology.text: Pictogram of a fetus (巳) in the womb (勹), or a swaddled baby.

funFacts: 红包 ‘red packet’ is money in a red envelope — the classic New Year gift.
pitfalls: A plastic bag is 塑料袋 or 袋子, not 包.
subtleties: 钱包 ‘money bag’ is a wallet; 包子 is a steamed filled bun.

profile.feeling: Tea, water, coffee — the drinking vessel of every kind.

examples.tr: The cup is on the table.

examples.py: Wǒ yào yí ge dà bēizi.

phrases.tr: a cup of water on a cartload of burning firewood
phrases.meaning: a hopelessly small effort for a big problem

phrases.tr: dry the cup

synonyms.nuance: a glass — when the material matters
in compounds and as the measure word ‘a cup of’: 一杯茶

etymology.text: 杯 (木 ‘wood’ + phonetic 不) + the toneless suffix 子.

funFacts: 干杯 ‘dry the cup’ is the Chinese ‘cheers!’ — traditionally you then empty it.
pitfalls: 杯子 is the cup itself; 杯 is the measure ‘a cup of’: 一个杯子 ‘a cup’, but 一杯茶 ‘a cup of tea’.
subtleties: Chinese does not split cup and glass as English does: any drinking vessel can be 杯子.

profile.feeling: Clear and fragile.

examples.py: Qǐng gěi wǒ yí ge bōlibēi.

examples.tr: He drinks tea from a glass.

synonyms.nuance: any cup or glass — the everyday word

etymology.text: 玻璃 ‘glass’ — an old loan from Prakrit phālia, Sanskrit sphaṭika ‘crystal’ — + 杯 ‘cup’.

funFacts: 玻璃 ‘glass’ came into Chinese from India: Sanskrit sphaṭika meant ‘crystal’.
pitfalls: In daily speech people simply say 杯子; 玻璃杯 is used when the material matters.
subtleties: 玻璃 has a toneless second syllable: bōli.

profile.feeling: Shared dishes in the middle of the table.

examples.tr: The plates are in the cupboard.
He works as a waiter in a restaurant.

collocations.tr: to carry plates; to work as a waiter

phrases.tr: to carry plates

synonyms.nuance: bowl — at a Chinese meal everyone has a bowl
the measure ‘a plate of’: 一盘饺子

etymology.text: 盘 (traditional 盤: phonetic 般 + 皿 ‘vessel’) + the toneless suffix 子.

funFacts: At a Chinese meal the dishes stand in the middle on 盘子, and each person eats from a bowl, 碗.
pitfalls: 盘子 is the plate; 盘 is the measure ‘a plate of’: 一个盘子 ‘a plate’, 一盘菜 ‘a plate of food’.
subtleties: 端盘子 ‘to carry plates’ is a colloquial way to say ‘to wait tables’.

lexemes.role: measure word for buildings and houses: 一栋房子, 一栋楼; 座 and 所 are also used for houses
measure word for rooms: 一间房子, 一间教室 (间 = ‘space between’)
measure word for doors and windows — panels that swing open, like a fan (扇子): 一扇门, 一扇窗户
measure word for flat surfaces you face: walls, mirrors, flags — 一面墙, 一面镜子
measure word for flat things and things with a flat top: tables, beds, paper, photos, tickets — 一张桌子, 一张纸
measure word for things held by a handle: chairs, keys, knives, umbrellas — 一把椅子, 一把钥匙
measure word for bound volumes: books, notebooks, magazines — 一本书
measure word for long thin things: pens, pencils, cigarettes — 一支笔
measure word for machines and works: phones, films, novels — 一部手机, 一部电影
measure word for lamps: 一盏灯
a container used as a measure: ‘a cup of, a glass of’ — 一杯茶, 一杯水; the cup itself is 杯子 (一个杯子)
